video_title: Cedric Coward Walk-Off Interview | Nets vs. Grizzlies

quotes.speaker: Cedric Coward
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Coward on the Grizzlies' collective energy and team culture
quotes.excerpt: That's part of our culture, that's part of who we are. Coach preaches it, players preach it.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Cedric, first of all, it was obviously a long day for everybody. How were you guys able to bring energy for four quarters tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Cedric Coward
text_blocks.text: That's what we need to be. That's part of our culture, that's part of who we are. Coach preaches it, players preach it, staff was preaching it. So before this game, we knew we were going to have to bring a little extra ump, and we did that today.

quotes.social_post: Cedric Coward on the Grizzlies team energy after a long day: That is part of our culture, that is part of who we are. Coach preaches it, players preach it, staff was preaching it.

structured.context: Cedric Coward discusses the Memphis Grizzlies team energy and culture following their game against the Brooklyn Nets.

quotes.speaker: Cedric Coward
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Coward on his rebounding approach and missing teammates
quotes.excerpt: I know without Zach today, without QP, without a couple guys, JG, Ty, we needed that rebounding.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Another double-double for you. Rebounding has been huge for you all season. How much of an emphasis have you put on that to try and do even more on that end?

text_blocks.speaker: Cedric Coward
text_blocks.text: That's always been who I am since I was little. Part of rebounding is see ball, get ball. You want to touch the ball. Plus, I know without Zach today, without QP, without a couple guys, JG, Ty, we needed that rebounding.

quotes.social_post: Cedric Coward on his rebounding mentality: Part of rebounding is see ball, get ball. You want to touch the ball.

structured.context: Cedric Coward explains his rebounding focus while noting the absence of several teammates during the post-game interview.

quotes.speaker: Cedric Coward
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Coward on his putback dunk and coaching feedback
quotes.excerpt: I got a clip from my personal coach, Coach Thorp. He showed me an opportunity I had.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Two plays I want to ask you about. One, the putback dunk on Jaylen's miss. You go over Deron Sharp, who was getting rebounds all night tonight. What made you think you could get over him and throw it down?

text_blocks.speaker: Cedric Coward
text_blocks.text: The previous game, I got a clip from my personal coach, Coach Thorp. He showed me an opportunity I had over a putback dunk and I didn't get it and I got boxed out. So he said, 'be more athletic.' So I made sure to go in this game making sure I was more athletic. Plus, Sharp was killing us on the boards all night. So at least get one of them out of his hands.

quotes.social_post: Cedric Coward says his personal coach told him to be more athletic after missing a putback opportunity in the previous game, leading to his dunk tonight.

structured.context: Cedric Coward describes a putback dunk and credits feedback from his personal coach for his improved athleticism on the boards.

quotes.speaker: Cedric Coward
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Coward on the alley-oop pass to Javon Small
quotes.excerpt: I see it every day in practice, and I was the only one that threw one to him.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Then the other one, the alley-oop pass to Javon Small. What made you think that he could get up there and throw that one down like he did?

text_blocks.speaker: Cedric Coward
text_blocks.text: I see it every day in practice, and I was the only one that threw one to him in Summer League. So I was like, let's get it now in the real season. I knew he was going to go get it. I thought it should have been an and-one, me personally, but he went and got it and shout out to him.

quotes.social_post: Cedric Coward on his alley-oop to Javon Small: I see it every day in practice, and I was the only one that threw one to him in Summer League. So I was like, let's get it now in the real season.

structured.context: Cedric Coward discusses his alley-oop pass to teammate Javon Small during the game.

quotes.speaker: Cedric Coward
quotes.summary_phrase: Cedric Coward on the Grizzlies' road dog mentality
quotes.excerpt: Watch the film, dissect what we can do better, and just take that road dog approach.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Back on the road this week. What do you guys want to take from these last couple of games and keep moving forward?

text_blocks.speaker: Cedric Coward
text_blocks.text: Watch the film, dissect what we can do better, because there is a lot of things we could have done better, not only in this game but in the New Orleans game as well. And just take that road dog approach. We have to. Bring the energy, bring that grit, and bring our own playstyle to wherever we play at.

quotes.social_post: Cedric Coward on the Grizzlies road trip: We have to take that road dog approach. Bring the energy, bring that grit, and bring our own playstyle to wherever we play at.

structured.context: Cedric Coward reflects on the team's upcoming road schedule and the need to improve based on recent game film.
